Yes: the closest match is a seed-guided clustering-by-exclusion method that starts from a few labeled markers and grows clusters by admitting only non-anomalous points, while naturally isolating fringe points, isolated noise, and possible unknown clusters [1]. It is designed specifically for noisy settings where you want to identify clusters by removing the “odd ones out,” and it reports strong results with as few as 10–30 seeds per cluster [1].

Related papers cover parts of the idea differently. PLSCAN and ToMAToMP also separate clusters from noise or outliers, but they are unsupervised and do not use starting markers; they focus on multiscale density persistence and topological robustness, respectively [4,10]. Another outlier-detection paper uses clustering plus visual expert criteria to detect outliers, but it is not a seed-guided cluster-growing method [7].
